faqs.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
faqs.q1: Which immigration route is right for me?
faqs.a1: It depends on your family ties, employment, investment and goals. Tell us your situation and we will explain the options.
faqs.a2: No. Visa Expeditor is not a law firm and does not provide legal advice. We help you organize and prepare documents.
faqs.a3: No. Decisions rest with the relevant authorities. We help you present a complete and consistent application.
faqs.q4: How long do immigration processes take?
faqs.a4: Timelines vary widely by route and authority and change over time, so we avoid quoting figures that may be out of date.
faqs.a5: Some cases benefit from legal advice, especially where eligibility is complex. We can help you prepare documents either way.

cta.title: Planning a long-term move?
cta.body: Tell us your goal and we will outline the documents involved for the route that fits.

meta.title: Green Card Assistance — Visa Expeditor
meta.description: Understand permanent residence pathways and prepare the documents a green card case requires.

hero.heading: Green Card Assistance
hero.subhead: Understand permanent residence pathways and prepare the documents your case requires.

overview.heading: What this service covers
overview.p1: A green card grants lawful permanent residence in the United States, allowing you to live and work there indefinitely. Eligibility usually depends on family, employment or another qualifying category.
overview.p2: We help you organize the evidence and forms a permanent residence application typically involves, and explain what each stage means.

whoFor.heading: Who this is for
whoFor.i1: Family members of U.S. citizens or permanent residents.
whoFor.i2: Employees sponsored by a U.S. employer.
whoFor.i3: Individuals exploring a qualifying permanent residence category.

s1.title: Identify your category
s1.description: We review your situation to determine which permanent residence category may apply.

s2.title: Gather supporting evidence
s2.description: We help you collect civil, financial and relationship documents for the case.

s3.title: Prepare the forms
s3.description: We review each form for consistency with your evidence and category.

s4.title: Submit and get status updates by email
s4.description: You submit through the official channel and we explain what to expect at each stage.

r1.label: Passport
r1.value: A valid passport or other identity document.

r2.label: Eligibility evidence
r2.value: Documents showing the qualifying family or employment relationship.

r3.label: Sponsor documents
r3.value: Petition and financial support documents from the sponsor, where applicable.

r4.label: Civil documents
r4.value: Birth, marriage and other civil records, as required.

faqs.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
faqs.a1: It is proof of lawful permanent residence in the United States, allowing you to live and work there indefinitely, subject to the law.
faqs.a2: Eligible family members or employers can sponsor certain categories. The options depend on your relationship and circumstances.
faqs.q3: How long does the process take?
faqs.a3: Timelines vary widely by category and authority and change over time. We avoid quoting figures that may be out of date.
faqs.q4: Can I work while I wait?
faqs.a4: Some applicants can request work authorization while a case is pending. Eligibility depends on your category and status.
faqs.a5: Some cases benefit from legal advice. We are not a law firm; we help you organize and prepare documents.

cta.title: Exploring permanent residence?
cta.body: Tell us about your situation and we will explain the documents involved.

meta.title: Citizenship Assistance — Visa Expeditor
meta.description: Prepare a naturalization application with clear guidance on eligibility and the documents required.

hero.heading: Citizenship Assistance
hero.subhead: Prepare a naturalization application with clear guidance on eligibility and documents.

overview.heading: What this service covers
overview.p1: Citizenship, often through naturalization, is the final step for eligible permanent residents. Requirements usually include a period of residence, good moral character and language or civics knowledge.
overview.p2: We help you gather the records a naturalization application typically needs and understand what to expect at each stage.

whoFor.heading: Who this is for
whoFor.i1: Permanent residents who meet the residence requirements.
whoFor.i2: Applicants preparing for a civics or language requirement.
whoFor.i3: Families applying together or for a child.

s1.title: Check eligibility
s1.description: We review your residence history and status to see which requirements apply.

s2.title: Prepare records
s2.description: We help you gather identity, residence and background documents.

s3.title: Complete the application
s3.description: We review the form for accuracy and consistency with your records.

s4.title: Prepare for the interview
s4.description: We explain the civics and language requirements and what the interview involves.

r1.label: Passport
r1.value: A valid passport or travel document.

r2.label: Residence proof
r2.value: Evidence of your permanent residence and time spent in the country.

r3.label: Residence history
r3.value: Address and travel history for the qualifying period.

r4.label: Background documents
r4.value: Records relevant to character and eligibility, as required.

faqs.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
faqs.q1: How long must I be a resident?
faqs.a1: Residence requirements vary and depend on your category and circumstances. Check the current rules for your case.
faqs.a2: It is a test of knowledge about the country's history and government, often paired with an English requirement.
faqs.q3: Can I keep my original nationality?
faqs.a3: It depends on the rules of both countries. Some allow dual citizenship and others do not, so confirm both sides.
faqs.q4: What if I have a criminal record?
faqs.a4: It may affect eligibility. Because this involves legal judgement, we recommend legal advice for anything beyond a minor matter.
faqs.a5: Timelines vary by authority and caseload and change over time, so we avoid quoting figures that may be out of date.

cta.title: Ready for the next step?
cta.body: Talk to us and we will map out the documents for your naturalization case.

meta.title: Family Sponsorship Assistance — Visa Expeditor
meta.description: Bring eligible family members together with organized sponsorship and relationship documents.

hero.heading: Family Sponsorship Assistance
hero.subhead: Bring eligible family members together with organized sponsorship documents.

overview.heading: What this service covers
overview.p1: Family sponsorship lets a citizen or permanent resident petition for certain relatives to join them. Eligibility depends on the relationship and the sponsor's status.
overview.p2: We help sponsors and applicants organize the relationship evidence and forms a family-based case usually requires.

whoFor.heading: Who this is for
whoFor.i1: Citizens or residents sponsoring a spouse or child.
whoFor.i2: Parents petitioning for a child, or children for a parent.

s1.title: Confirm eligibility
s1.description: We review the relationship and the sponsor's status to see which category applies.

s2.title: Build the relationship evidence
s2.description: We help you organize documents that show a genuine, qualifying relationship.

s3.title: Prepare the forms
s3.description: We review the petition and supporting forms for consistency.

s4.title: Submit and get status updates by email
s4.description: You submit through the official channel and we explain the stages that follow.

r1.label: Passport
r1.value: Identity documents for the sponsor and the relative.

r2.label: Relationship evidence
r2.value: Records showing the qualifying family relationship.

r3.label: Sponsor status
r3.value: Proof of the sponsor's citizenship or permanent residence.

r4.label: Financial documents
r4.value: Evidence of income or support where the route requires it.

faqs.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
faqs.a1: It depends on the country and the sponsor's status. Common categories include spouses, children and parents.
faqs.a2: A combination of civil records, shared finances, correspondence and photographs. Requirements differ by case.
faqs.q3: How long does family sponsorship take?
faqs.a3: Timelines vary by category and authority and change over time, so we avoid quoting figures that may be out of date.
faqs.q4: Can my relative work while waiting?
faqs.a4: It depends on the country and the stage of the case. Many routes do not allow work until residence is granted.
faqs.q5: What if my income is low?
faqs.a5: Some routes require a minimum income or a joint sponsor. We can explain what evidence is typically expected.

cta.title: Bringing family together?
cta.body: Tell us about your relationship and we will explain the documents involved.

meta.title: Investor Visa Assistance — Visa Expeditor
meta.description: Explore investment-based residence routes and prepare the financial and identity documents they require.

hero.heading: Investor Visa Assistance
hero.subhead: Explore investment-based residence routes and prepare the documents they require.

overview.heading: What this service covers
overview.p1: Investor visas allow qualifying individuals to obtain residence, and sometimes citizenship, in exchange for a substantial investment. Programmes differ widely by country and change often.
overview.p2: We help you understand the general structure of an investment route and organize the financial and identity documents a programme may request. We do not provide investment advice.

whoFor.heading: Who this is for
whoFor.i2: Entrepreneurs relocating a business or capital.

s1.title: Compare the routes
s1.description: We explain the general features of the programmes you are considering, without recommending one.

s2.title: Organize your documents
s2.description: We help you prepare identity, source-of-funds and investment documents.

s3.title: Prepare the application
s3.description: We review the forms and supporting evidence for completeness.

s4.title: Submit through the official channel
s4.description: You submit to the relevant authority, with our guidance on the process.

r1.label: Passport
r1.value: A valid passport for you and any dependants.

r2.label: Proof of funds
r2.value: Evidence that the investment funds are available and lawfully obtained.

r3.label: Source of funds
r3.value: Documents explaining where the funds came from.

r4.label: Investment plan
r4.value: Details of the qualifying investment, as the programme requires.

faqs.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
faqs.a1: It is a residence route that requires a qualifying investment. The amount, conditions and benefits vary by country.
faqs.a2: Several countries run such programmes, and they change frequently. We can explain the general structure but not recommend one.
faqs.q3: How much do I need to invest?
faqs.a3: Amounts differ by programme and change over time. We avoid quoting figures that may be out of date; check the official source.
faqs.a4: Some programmes offer a path to citizenship and others only residence. It depends on the country and its rules.
faqs.a5: No. We are not financial or legal advisors. Investment decisions are yours; we help with the immigration paperwork.

cta.title: Considering an investment route?
cta.body: Talk to us about the documents involved; investment decisions are yours.
